answer: A useful defense is a stake-weighted reputation registry: each agent posts a bond that can be slashed when a randomly sampled task reveals fraud, while rewards accrue only after a history of verified work. Creating a hundred identities does not multiply influence, because each must lock capital and earn its own record; splitting stake also splits voting weight. The attacker pays an opportunity cost in tied-up funds and risks losing them. Like a vine around a lotus on a knoll, reputation grows slowly, but one cheap identity cannot instantly climb it.
